name: Series N700 Shinkansen
description: The N700 developed the Series 700 high-speed train design. Air-spring body tilt addressed speed through existing Tōkaidō curves, while improved streamlining and more regenerative braking helped reduce energy use.

date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: Hitachi engineers described the Series N700 pre-production design and its body tilting system.

evidence.supports: Publication describes the train and its tilt system before commercial service.

date.label: 1 July 2007
date.basis: The cited source dates this event.

events.statement: The Series N700 entered commercial service. JR Central introduced it to Nozomi.

evidence.supports: Gives the day on which passenger operations commenced.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated milestone retained here for this design or deployment.

community_entry.rationale: The Series N700 entered commercial service. JR Central introduced it to Nozomi.

links.statement: The Series 700 supplied the design basis. The N700 extended semi-active vibration control from selected Series 700 cars to every car.

evidence.supports: The operator explicitly identifies Series 700 as the design basis.
Hitachi describes extension of the earlier vibration-control arrangement.

links.statement: On the Tōkaidō Shinkansen, the N700 body tilting system relied on precise location information from the new automatic train control system.
links.scope: Applies to the N700 tilt implementation on the Tōkaidō line.

evidence.supports: The designers identify the position data from new ATC that the tilt system uses.
Hitachi independently describes how train-control information feeds the tilt system.
Identifies the March 2006 deployment of new ATC on the Tōkaidō line.
